01 / Research & Technology

Exploring Virtual Acoustics Algorithms in the SpatialScaper Framework: Effects on Sound Event Localization Model Training

My master’s thesis investigated how simulated room acoustics shape the synthetic audio used to train machines to locate and identify sounds. Working within SpatialScaper, the research examined the Image Source Method (ISM), Scattering Delay Networks (SDN), and hybrid reverberation approaches. The central question was how these choices in dataset generation affect sound event localization and detection (SELD) model performance — connecting the character of a virtual acoustic space with what a listening system learns.

Master’s thesis researcher

02 / Research & Technology

Cadenza CLIP2 Audio Machine Learning Experiments

These independent experiments use the Cadenza CLIP2 baseline and dataset to investigate lyric intelligibility prediction: how understandable sung words may be to a listener. The work examines audio representations, regression models, and hearing-loss severity information, bringing together signal-based features and listener-related context. It reflects my broader interest in how machine learning can describe aspects of musical listening. This is independent exploratory work, rather than a competition submission or a claim of published challenge results.

Independent audio machine learning experiments

03 / Software & Development

Voice Denoiser — Real-Time ML Noise Reduction

I built a real-time speech-denoising plugin in C++ and JUCE, embedding RNNoise’s pretrained neural model directly inside a native VST3 audio effect. It supports mono and stereo audio, with a latency-aligned dry/wet control for adjusting the amount of processed signal. Input/output meters and separate displays for plugin latency and RNNoise processing time make the audio pipeline visible. The project connects machine-learning-based speech enhancement with practical audio-tool development.

C++ · JUCE · RNNoise integration

04 / Software & Development

Three-Band Compressor — Capstone Project

For my capstone, I developed a three-band compressor for controlling audio dynamics across low, mid, and high frequency bands. The interface includes adjustable crossover points, attack, release, threshold, and ratio controls, alongside input/output gain and a spectrum display. The project connects audio signal processing and software development with practical music-production tools.
